nodes.name: Electrodeposition of ε-MnO2 on CP
nodes.procedure: ε-MnO2 was grown in situ on hydrophilic, functionalized carbon paper (CP) through electrodeposition.
nodes.source_text: ε-MnO2 was grown in situ on hydrophilic, functionalized CP through electrodeposition (Figure S3).

nodes.name: Cation exchange and annealing of ε-MnO2
nodes.procedure: The resulting ε-MnO2 was then immersed in an aqueous RuCl3 solution to initiate cation exchange.[33,34] Subsequently, the product was annealed at 350°C to form an anhydrous Ru/MnO2 nanosheet catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM and TEM confirm Ru/MnO2 retains nanosheet morphology of ε-MnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images confirm that Ru/MnO2 retains the nanosheet morphology characteristic of ε-MnO2 (Figure 1a and Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM measurements reveal Ru/MnO2 nanosheets possess thickness of approximately 1.4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements reveal that these nanosheets possess a thickness of approximately 1.4 nm (Figure 1b and Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms atomic isolation of Ru single atoms within Ru/MnO2 lattice, replacing Mn sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) confirms the atomic isolation of Ru single atoms within the Ru/MnO2 (Figure 1c and Figure S13).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn 2p XPS of Ru/MnO2 shows 0.28 eV upshift vs pristine ε-MnO2; Ru 3p shows 0.31 eV positive shift vs RuO2 indicating electron transfer from Mn to Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mn 2p XPS spectrum of Ru/MnO2 exhibits a discernible upshift of approximately 0.28 eV in contrast to pristine ε-MnO2 ... The corresponding Ru 3p XPS spectra ... overall binding energy of the Ru/MnO2 is 0.31 eV positive shift ... commercial RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn K-edge XANES shows higher oxidation state of Mn in Ru/MnO2 vs MnO2; Ru K-edge shows negative shift confirming reduced Ru oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) of Ru/MnO2 reveals a near-edge absorption energy slightly higher than that of MnO2 ... This is further corroborated by the negative shift in the absorption energy of the Ru K-edge XANES (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn K-edge EXAFS shows Mn-O at 1.44 Å and Mn-O-Ru shift to 2.42 Å; Ru K-edge shows Ru-O at 1.46 Å (CN=5.6) vs 1.50 Å in RuO2, no Ru-Ru peak confirming atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the Mn K-edge, both MnO2 and Ru/MnO2 exhibited a dominant peak at 1.44 Å ... the peak at 2.40 Å ... shifted to 2.42 Å in Ru/MnO2 ... the EXAFS spectra at the Ru K-edge revealed ... Ru-O coordination shell ... reduced to 1.46 Å ... Quantitative R-space fitting showed ... coordination number (CN) of Ru-O in Ru/MnO2 was 5.6.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPR shows reduction temperature of Mn species in Ru/MnO2 decreased from 307°C to 215°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Hydrogen temperature-programmed reduction (H2-TPR) tests revealed that the reduction temperature of Mn species in the Ru/MnO2 catalyst decreased from 307 to 215°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ru/MnO2 and MnO2 align with ε-MnO2 standard (JCPDS No. 30-0820), no Ru peaks indicating high dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction patterns of both the Ru/MnO2 and MnO2 samples align with the standard pattern for ε-MnO2 (ref 35, JCPDS No. 30-0820), with no detectable peaks corresponding to Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ru/MnO2 MnO6 peaks stable up to 1.8 V vs RHE with no MnVIIO4- formation, unlike ε-MnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, the characteristic Raman peaks of MnO6 Ru/MnO2 do not shift with increasing potential, and no MnVIIO4- species were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XRD shows Ru/MnO2 sustains 90% peak intensity of (100) and (101) planes throughout 1.35-1.70 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the quantitative findings reveal a swift decline in peak intensity for both (100) and (101) in ε-MnO2, whereas the Ru/MnO2 sustains 90% peak intensity throughout the voltage range of 1.35-1.70 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS shows Ru-OO* intermediate peak at 1124 cm⁻¹ at 1.6 V for Ru/MnO2 indicating LOM pathway.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under a 1.6 V bias, a prominent absorption peak was observed at 1124 cm⁻¹, attributed to a key Ru-OO* intermediate, which is indicative of the LOM pathway.

nodes.characterization_summary: 18O isotope-labeling DEMS confirms LOM in Ru/MnO2 with significant 34O2 production vs minimal in ε-MnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) values of 34 and 36 observed during the OER of Ru/MnO2 indicated the presence of 34O2 (18O16O) and 36O2 (18O18O) in the gas production.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Ru/MnO2 is 72 m²/g and ε-MnO2 is 44 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The interconnected 3D ultrathin nanosheet network and smaller mesopores result in a large surface area (72 m²/g for Ru/MnO2 and 44 m²/g for ε-MnO2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacings of 0.21 nm and 0.24 nm corresponding to (101) and (100) planes of ε-MnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The images obtained from high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveal lattice spacings of 0.21 and 0.24 nm, corresponding to the (101) and (100) lattice planes of ε-MnO2, respectively (Figure S10).

nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) reveal that the elemental distribution of Ru is consistent with the Mn and O elemental mapping signals (Figure S16).
